question:
A teacher records the number of questions correctly solved by two study groups in three activity sets during two practice sessions. The first-session record is $A=\begin{bmatrix}4&6&5\\3&7&4\end{bmatrix}$ and the second-session record is $B=\begin{bmatrix}5&4&6\\6&3&5\end{bmatrix}$. Rows correspond to the two groups and columns correspond to the three activity sets. For another comparison, the teacher uses the column matrix $W=\begin{bmatrix}2\\3\\1\end{bmatrix}$, whose entries represent the weights assigned to the three activity sets. The students investigate which matrix operations are possible, combine the records from the two sessions, form a scalar-based comparison, and use matrix multiplication to obtain a weighted total for each group.

(a) State the orders of $A$, $B$ and $W$. Determine which of $A+B$, $AW$ and $WA$ are defined.

(b) Calculate $A+B$.

(c) Evaluate $2A-B$.

(d) Calculate $AW$ and interpret the two entries of the product.
explanation:
(a)
Matrices $A$ and $B$ each have 2 rows and 3 columns, so their order is $2\times3$. Matrix $W$ has 3 rows and 1 column, so its order is $3\times1$. Since $A$ and $B$ have the same order, $A+B$ is defined and has order $2\times3$. For $AW$, the number of columns of $A$ is 3 and the number of rows of $W$ is 3, so $AW$ is defined and has order $2\times1$. For $WA$, $W$ has 1 column while $A$ has 2 rows. Since $1\ne2$, $WA$ is not defined.

(b)
Matrix addition is performed by adding corresponding entries. Therefore, $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}4+5&6+4&5+6\\3+6&7+3&4+5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}9&10&11\\9&10&9\end{bmatrix}$.

(c)
First, $2A=\begin{bmatrix}8&12&10\\6&14&8\end{bmatrix}$. Hence, $2A-B=\begin{bmatrix}8-5&12-4&10-6\\6-6&14-3&8-5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3&8&4\\0&11&3\end{bmatrix}$.

(d)
Using row-by-column multiplication, $AW=\begin{bmatrix}4&6&5\\3&7&4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2\\3\\1\end{bmatrix}$. The first entry is $4(2)+6(3)+5(1)=8+18+5=31$. The second entry is $3(2)+7(3)+4(1)=6+21+4=31$. Therefore, $AW=\begin{bmatrix}31\\31\end{bmatrix}$. The two entries are the weighted totals for the first and second study groups respectively. Thus, both groups obtain the same weighted total of 31.

options.A:
(a) $A,B$ are $2\times3$ and $W$ is $3\times1$; $A+B$, $AW$ and $WA$ are all defined.
(b) $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}9&10&11\\9&10&9\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) $2A-B=\begin{bmatrix}3&8&4\\0&11&3\end{bmatrix}$.
(d) $AW=\begin{bmatrix}31\\31\end{bmatrix}$.
options.B:

(c) $2A-B=\begin{bmatrix}3&8&4\\0&11&3\end{bmatrix}$.
